messages:
anya: quick sync - discovered a routing/staleness gap during the new eviction fast-path rollout. filing notes and owners here.
samir: saw a spike in read errors on the canary, looked related to prefix routing. what was the exact mismatch?
anya: router hands out residency tokens (epoch ids). the fast demote was swapping epoch on node A but there was a brief window where the router still sent reads to node B using the old epoch. node B treated the token as stale and returned an error.
kevin: hmm, different from tombstone delivery - this is a router-token visibility problem.
tle: could routers validate epochs then failover to read-through proxy instead of returning 5xx? that pushes correctness into routing rather than forcing sync across replicas.
anya: that's one option. tradeoff: more routing complexity and extra hop (proxy adds latency) vs forcing demote to block until local materialize (adds latency to demote ops).
samir: proposal for short-term mitigation: implement router-side soft-failover. when a node rejects a token as stale, the router retries to the read-through path (no 5xx) and increments a metric. cheap and reversible.
kevin: good for immediate safety. telemetry should count stale-token hits per-prefix and per-node; alert if retry rate spikes.
tle: long-term: two architectural paths to choose from - (A) stronger demote durability (sync local materialize + publish epoch swap, heavier demote), (B) router-aware epoch handshake (routers keep small cache of recent epoch swaps and use read-through fallback). both aim to avoid cross-node leases.
anya: owners: samir will ship the router soft-failover patch behind flag, tle will add a deterministic chaos test that stalls the demote ack, and i'll own the demote durability exploration doc.
samir: patch sketch: on 401-like epoch rejection from node -> router routes to read-through proxy (same request), add tag "fallback=epoch_mismatch" to tracing, increment metric "prefetch.epoch_mismatch_fallback" and set header X-RW-Epoch-Retry.
kevin: please ensure the router does at most one retry and does not retry loops. also surface the original node id in traces.
tle: test plan: harness will simulate delayed local tombstone materialization and assert router fallback happened and no 5xx returned. will also assert metric emitted exactly once per request.
anya: infra-bot: rollback happened earlier in staging; please run the new-canary test once soft-failover is deployed.
infra-bot: rollback completed by @deploy-bot at 07:30 UTC.
anya: timeline: samir - ship soft-failover PR today EOD behind flag; tle - chaos test + harness by midweek; i'll draft the durability vs router-handshake decision doc for Friday arch sync.
kevin: keep rollback plan and feature flag. prefer router-fallback short-term so demote latency stays low.
samir: understood. small snippet of router logic: \n```\nresp = send_to_node(req, node)\nif resp.code == EPOCH_MISMATCH and not req.headers["X-RW-Epoch-Retry"]:\n  metrics.inc("prefetch.epoch_mismatch_fallback")\n  req.headers["X-RW-Epoch-Retry"] = "1"\n  return send_to_read_through_proxy(req)\nelse:\n  return resp\n```\nanya: thanks. will follow up with links to PRs + canary results.
